chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: Six months as Carlos Gastell's partner managing singers
summary: After breaking up the 1949 band he spent about six months at Gastell's management firm, whose clients included Peggy Lee, Mel Torme and Nat Cole, and found it boring.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Okay. How long did you stay in business with Carlos? Did you say it was about eight months?

Oh, maybe six months. It's hard to -- I found it very boring, very boring and irritating, and Carlos was a one man operation. Carlos never needed a partner of any kind. I mean he was a dynamo of a man, I mean in handling

the people he handled, and I think he realized I needed some sort of a thing, you know, a cushion to land on, after what I had done, and he provided it. I'm sure he didn't need me. I was very happy, though. At the time being it was something to do, give me a chance to sit down and think things out.

Oh, Peggy Lee. We had Mel Torme. We had Nat Cole. We had Nellie Lutcher. We had Rafael Mendez. We had -- oh, let's see, there's something I'm forgetting there. Oh, June Hutton. And Woody Herman. So, you know, it was an interesting stable. I mean they're all people that you could be proud to say, "I represent them."
